The hardest part, he says, was not the distance but the (4) ___ : it rained for nine days without stopping. He (5) ___ people from more than twenty countries, and he still keeps in (6) ___ with some of them.

items.why: complete a walk. 'succeeded' needs 'in + -ing'; 'arrived' needs 'at/in'.
manage TO do something. The others are not followed by 'to find' with this meaning.
stay in a hostel / hotel (for a short time).
Weather = what happens on particular days (rain). Climate is the general pattern of a place.
meet people = see them for the first time. 'Knew' is a false friend of 'conocer' here.
keep in touch with = seguir en contacto con.

reading.title: Part 5 · Choose the word (text 2)
reading.intro: Choose the correct word for each gap.
reading.text:
OUR SCHOOL GARDEN

Two years ago, the piece of land behind our school was full of rubbish. Then our science teacher (1) ___ that we turn it into a garden. At first nobody was very (2) ___ on the idea, but she persuaded us to try. We (3) ___ money by selling cakes, and a local company gave us tools. Now we (4) ___ tomatoes, beans and herbs, and the school canteen uses them. Looking after the garden takes (5) ___ a lot of our free time, but nobody complains. It has (6) ___ a real difference to our school.

items.why: suggest THAT somebody does something. 'told' and 'advised' need a person: told us / advised us.
keen ON. (interested IN, excited ABOUT, fond OF)
raise money = recaudar dinero. 'Rise' never has an object.
grow vegetables. 'Grow up' is for children becoming adults.
take up time/space = ocupar.
make a difference.

listening.title: Part 1 · Short recordings
listening.intro: You will hear five short recordings. Read the question and the three options FIRST, then press Play. In the exam you hear everything twice. Tip: all three options are usually mentioned. Listen for the one that answers the question.

script.t: Did you get anything for Dad's birthday?
Well, I looked at some ties, but he's got hundreds. Then I saw a lovely wallet, but it was far too expensive. In the end I got him that book about mountains he keeps talking about.
Good choice. He'll love it.

items.q: What did the boy buy for his father?
items.why: Ties: 'he's got hundreds'. Wallet: 'far too expensive'. 'In the end I got him that book.'

script.t: Hi Sara, it's Ben. About tomorrow: the film starts at quarter past seven, not half past six as I told you. So let's meet outside the cinema at seven. That gives us fifteen minutes to buy popcorn. See you then!

items.why: 6.30 was the wrong time he gave before; 7.15 is when the film starts; they MEET at seven.

script.t: And now the weather for tomorrow. The morning will start cold and foggy, so take care on the roads. By lunchtime the fog will have gone and we can expect sunshine for the rest of the day. The rain we promised you will not arrive until Thursday.

items.q: What will the weather be like tomorrow afternoon?
items.why: Fog is only in the morning; rain arrives on Thursday; 'sunshine for the rest of the day'.

script.t: How was your trip to the coast? Did you drive?
We were going to, but the car broke down the day before. There's no train station there, so in the end we took the coach. It was actually really comfortable.

items.q: How did the woman travel to the coast?
items.why: The car broke down, there is no station, 'in the end we took the coach'.

script.t: Excuse me, is there a chemist's near here?
Yes. Go straight on past the bank, and turn left at the traffic lights. It's next to the post office, opposite the park.
Left at the lights. Thanks very much.

items.why: You walk PAST the bank. It is 'next to the post office, opposite the park'.

listening.title: Part 2 · Short conversations
listening.intro: You will hear four short conversations. These questions are about opinions and feelings, so the answer is not one word you hear. Tip: listen for 'but', 'actually', 'to be honest'. The real opinion usually comes after them.

script.t: So what did you think of the new sports centre?
Well, everyone told me it was expensive, but the price seemed fine to me. And the pool is fantastic. The only thing is, it took me forty minutes to get there, and I had to change buses twice.
Oh, that's a pity.

items.q: What does the boy dislike about the sports centre?
items.why: The price 'seemed fine', the pool is 'fantastic'. 'The only thing is' introduces the problem: the journey.

script.t: Have you finished the history project?
Nearly. To be honest, I thought it would be really boring, but once I started reading about the castle, I couldn't stop. I even went to see it on Sunday.
Wow. I still haven't started mine.

items.q: How does the girl feel about the project?
opts: She found it more interesting than she expected.
She is worried that she will not finish it.
She thinks it is too much work.
items.why: 'I thought it would be really boring, BUT... I couldn't stop.'

script.t: Are you coming to Jake's party on Saturday?
I'd love to, but my cousins are visiting from Ireland and Mum wants me at home. I asked if I could go for just an hour, and she said no.
That's a shame. I'll tell Jake.

items.q: Why can't the boy go to the party?
opts: He has to travel to Ireland.
He has to stay with his family.
items.why: His cousins are coming FROM Ireland, and his mum wants him at home.

script.t: I'm thinking of buying these headphones. What do you think?
They look great, and the sound is amazing. But have you read the reviews? Lots of people say they break after a few months. If I were you, I'd keep looking.

items.q: What does the girl advise the boy to do?
items.why: 'If I were you, I'd keep looking' = do not buy these, look for others. She never mentions the price.

listening.title: Part 3 · Complete the notes (1)
listening.intro: You will hear a teacher giving information about a school trip. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time in each gap. Tip: read the notes first and decide what KIND of word is missing (a day? a price? a place?). The answers come in order.

script.t: Good morning, everyone. I want to give you some details about our trip to the Science Museum. We are going on Wednesday the twelfth of March. Please be at the school gate by eight fifteen, because the coach leaves at half past eight and it will not wait for anyone.

The trip costs fourteen pounds. That includes the coach and your ticket, but it does not include lunch, so you must bring a packed lunch with you. In the morning we will visit the space exhibition, and in the afternoon there is a workshop about robots, which I am sure you will enjoy.

You do not need to wear your uniform, but please wear comfortable shoes, because we will be walking a lot. Finally, I need the permission form, signed by your parents, by Friday. Give it to Mr Dalton. That is D, A, L, T, O, N. Thank you.

items.q: Date of the trip: Wednesday ___ March
items.why: 'Wednesday the twelfth of March'
8.15 is when students must be at the gate. The coach LEAVES at half past eight.
fourteen (14), not forty (40). Listen for the stress: fourTEEN.
'it does not include lunch, so you must bring a packed lunch'
Space is the morning exhibition. The afternoon workshop is about robots.
Spelt out: D-A-L-T-O-N. Practise the alphabet: A /ei/, E /i:/, I /ai/.

listening.title: Part 3 · Complete the notes (2)
listening.intro: You will hear a man talking on the radio about a photography competition for young people. Complete the notes.

script.t: If you are between eleven and seventeen and you love taking photos, listen carefully. Our young photographer competition is back. Last year the subject was animals. This year we want your best pictures of water. It could be the sea, the rain, or even a glass on your kitchen table.

You can send up to three photos. Please do not post them to us. Upload them on our website before the thirtieth of April. The winner will receive a new camera, and the second prize is a one-day course with a professional photographer.

The best twenty pictures will be shown in an exhibition at the city library during the month of June. If you have any questions, call us on oh one six three, four double five, nine seven two. Good luck!

items.why: Animals was LAST year. 'This year we want your best pictures of water.'
'up to three photos'
thirtieth (30th), not thirteenth (13th).
The course is the SECOND prize.
'an exhibition at the city library'. Remember: library = biblioteca.
'four double five, nine seven two' = 455 972. 'Double five' = 55.

listening.title: Part 4 · Interview
listening.intro: You will hear an interview with a young chef called Maya Ford. Read all six questions first. Tip: the questions follow the order of the interview, and each question starts when the interviewer asks something new.

script.t: Today I am talking to Maya Ford, who at only nineteen is already working as a chef in a top restaurant. Maya, when did you start cooking?
People think I learned from my mum, but she hates cooking! It was my neighbour, an old Italian lady. I used to go to her flat after school, and she let me help her make pasta. I was about eight.
And what was your first job in a kitchen like?

Hard! I was sixteen and I worked at weekends. I did not mind washing hundreds of plates, and the heat was fine. What I found really difficult was the speed. Everyone was shouting and running, and I was always too slow.
What do you enjoy most about your work now?

The money is not great, to be honest, and I almost never meet the customers. For me, it is creating new dishes. When the head chef puts one of my ideas on the menu, that is the best feeling in the world.
Is there anything you do not like?
The hours. I finish after midnight, so I hardly ever see my friends. They have stopped inviting me to things, which makes me a bit sad.
What advice would you give to young people who want to be chefs?

A lot of people say you must go to an expensive cookery school. I did not. My advice is to get a job in a real kitchen, any kitchen, as early as you can. You learn more in a month there than in a year of classes.
And finally, what are your plans?
Everybody expects me to say I want my own restaurant. Maybe one day. But first I am going to spend a year in Japan. I have already bought the ticket. I want to learn how they prepare fish there.

items.why: Her mum 'hates cooking'. 'It was my neighbour, an old Italian lady.'

items.q: What was the hardest thing about her first job?
items.why: She 'did not mind' the plates and the heat 'was fine'. 'What I found really difficult was the speed.'

items.q: What does Maya like most about her job now?
items.why: 'creating new dishes' = inventing. The money 'is not great' and she almost never meets customers.

items.q: What is the disadvantage of her job?
opts: She has to get up very early.
She has little time for her friends.
She does not get on with the head chef.
items.why: She finishes after midnight and hardly ever sees her friends.

items.q: What does Maya advise young people to do?
opts: go to a good cookery school
start working in a kitchen as soon as possible
items.why: 'get a job in a real kitchen... as early as you can'. She did NOT go to cookery school.

items.q: What is Maya going to do next?
items.why: 'first I am going to spend a year in Japan'. The restaurant is only 'maybe one day'.

guide.title: Reading Part 6: what it is
points: A short text (an email, a message, a short article) with 6 gaps. There are NO options: you write ONE word in each gap. 6 marks.

It tests grammar words, not difficult vocabulary. About nine gaps in ten are one of these: articles (a, an, the), prepositions (in, on, at, of, for, to, with), auxiliary verbs (is, was, have, been, do, will, would), pronouns (it, there, them, which, who), quantifiers (much, many, few, some, any, every), linking words (because, although, but, so, if, when, than, as) and small words from phrasal verbs and fixed phrases (look forward TO, at LEAST, instead OF).
Spelling must be correct. Contractions (don't, isn't) count as two words, so they are never the answer.

guide.title: Reading Part 6: the method (5 steps)
points: 1. Read the whole text quickly first, without writing. You need to know what it is about and whether it is past, present or future.
2. For each gap, read the WHOLE sentence, not only the three words around the gap. Look at what comes AFTER the gap as well as before.

3. Ask: what KIND of word is missing? Before a noun: article, quantifier or possessive (a, the, some, my). Before a past participle (given, made, been): an auxiliary (was, has, be). After an adjective or verb: probably a preposition (good AT, depend ON). Between two ideas: a linking word. After a noun plus comma: a relative pronoun (who, which, where, whose).
4. Write the word, then read the sentence again 'aloud in your head'. Does it sound right? Is the verb singular or plural? Is the tense the same as the rest of the text?
5. Never leave a gap empty. If you have no idea, write the most common small word that fits the kind of word you need (the, of, to, it, was).

guide.title: Reading Part 6: typical traps for Spanish speakers
points: Subjects cannot disappear in English: '___ is important to...' = IT; '___ are many people' = THERE.

Prepositions that are different from Spanish: depend ON, married TO, think ABOUT/OF, arrive AT/IN (never 'to'), on foot, by car, at the weekend, in the morning but on Monday morning, good AT, interested IN, keen ON.
for / since / ago: FOR six months, SINCE 2019, six months AGO.
so / such: SO tired, SUCH a good film, so MANY people, so MUCH time.
Comparisons: bigger THAN, as big AS, the same AS, THE best.
make / do, and other common verbs: make a mistake, make friends, make a decision, do homework, do sport, take a photo, take part, have a shower, it TAKES ten minutes.
who / which / where / whose: after a comma never use 'that'.
used TO live, look forward TO seeing, would LIKE to, had BETTER go, would RATHER stay.

guide.title: Listening: how to get better
points: Before each recording you have time. USE IT: read the questions, underline key words and think of other ways to say the options. The recording will almost never use the same words as the correct option.

In Parts 1, 2 and 4 all the options are usually mentioned. Wrong options are rejected ('too expensive', 'we were going to, but...') or belong to another time or person. Listen for the change of direction: but, actually, in the end, instead, to be honest, the only thing is.
You hear everything twice. First time: choose an answer. Second time: check it, and prove to yourself why the other two are wrong.

Part 3 (notes): decide what kind of word is missing before you listen. Train numbers (14 / 40, 13th / 30th), times, dates, prices and spelling of names. Write what you hear: usually one or two words. Small spelling mistakes in difficult words are accepted, but spelt-out names and easy words must be right.
If you miss an answer, forget it and go on. Losing one mark is fine; losing three because you were still thinking about it is not.

Daily training, 10 minutes: one dictation sentence set in this app, plus a short video or podcast in English with English subtitles. First listen without text, then with the text, then again without it.

guide.title: The other reading parts in one line each
points: Part 1 (5 short notices and messages): ask 'who is writing to whom, and why?'. The answer says the same thing in other words.
Part 2 (match 5 people with 8 texts): underline each person's two or three needs. The right text matches all of them; the traps match only one or two.
Part 3 (long text, 5 questions with 4 options): the questions follow the text in order. Find the exact line that proves the answer. Careful with what the writer EXPECTED and what really happened.
Part 4 (5 missing sentences, 8 options): look for links: pronouns (it, they, this, one), linking words (however, so, that is why) and time words.
Part 5 (choose 1 of 4 words, 6 gaps): it tests vocabulary and collocations. Look at the preposition after the gap and the noun that goes with the verb.
Timing for the whole Reading paper (45 minutes): about 7 minutes per part, and 3 minutes to check that every answer is on the answer sheet.
